exams.name: Board examination by Oregon Board of Optometry
exams.notes: Covers anatomy of the eye, pharmaceutical agents, refractive/accommodative/muscular conditions, subjective and objective optometry, lens fitting, principles of lens grinding and frame adjusting, and other subjects pertaining to optometry.
exams.quote: Any person who has signified to the Oregon Board of Optometry a desire to be examined by it and who has filed proof that the person is qualified under ORS 683.010 to 683.340 and the rules of the board to take the examination shall pay a fee to be determined by the board.

exams.name: National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO)
exams.notes: The board may, in its discretion, require the NBEO certificate in lieu of its own examination in one or more areas.
exams.quote: The board may, in its discretion, require the certificate of successful examination of the National Board of Examiners in Optometry in one or more areas of the examination in lieu of its examination in such areas.

exams.name: Pharmaceutical agents examination
exams.notes: Required for any person who petitions to prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents who has not previously been examined by the board on such use.
exams.quote: Any person who petitions the board to prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents who has not previously been examined by the board on such use shall pass an examination on the use and potential side effect of such agents as used in optometry

exams.name: Oregon optometric law and administrative rules (jurisprudence) examination
exams.notes: Required for applicants seeking licensure by endorsement from another state.
exams.quote: Passes a written examination approved by the board on Oregon optometric law and administrative rules

required.quote: All optometrists licensed in the State of Oregon are and shall be required to satisfactorily complete courses of study and satisfactorily continue their education by other means as determined by the Oregon Board of Optometry

definition_quote.value: the use of any means other than invasive or laser surgery, or the prescription of Schedule I and II drugs or pharmaceutical agents that are not on the optometric nontopical formulary, for diagnosis and treatment in the human eye, for the measurement or assistance of the powers or range of human vision or the determination of the accommodative and refractive states of the human eye or the scope of its functions in general or the adaptation of lenses or frames for the aid thereof, subject to the limitations of ORS 683.040.
